name: Chicken, rice & broccoli meal-prep bowls
desc: Soy-glazed chicken with capsicum, broccoli and basmati rice, portioned for the week.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it with 600 ml water, covered, on low heat for 12-15 minutes, then rest 5 minutes.
Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and season with salt, pepper, garlic and paprika.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 7-9 minutes until no pink remains and the thickest piece reaches 74 °C.
Add the sliced capsicum and broccoli florets with a splash of water, cover and steam for 4 minutes.
Stir through the soy sauce and divide the chicken, vegetables and rice evenly between four containers.
storage: Cool within 1 hour and refrigerate in sealed containers for up to 3-4 days, or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat until piping hot throughout.
subs: Use tamari for a gluten-free version.
Swap chicken for firm tofu (same weight) for a vegetarian bowl.
Use cauliflower rice to lower the carbohydrate count.
Use halal-certified chicken.
Choose a soy sauce or tamari with no added alcohol if you follow a strict halal diet.

name: Lean beef & bean chilli
desc: A rich, smoky chilli of lean beef mince, kidney beans and tomatoes served with rice.
steps: Dice the onion and capsicum.
Brown the mince in the oil over high heat for 5-6 minutes, breaking it up; drain excess fat if needed.
Add the onion and capsicum and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the spices (chilli, cumin, paprika) for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and drained beans, simmer uncovered for 25-30 minutes until thick.
Serve each portion with 150 g cooked rice.
storage: Keeps 4 days refrigerated or 3 months frozen. Freeze the chilli and rice separately for best texture.
subs: Use halal-certified beef mince.
Turkey mince works for a leaner option.
Replace the mince with extra beans and lentils for a vegetarian chilli.

name: High-protein overnight oats
desc: Creamy no-cook oats soaked overnight with yoghurt, milk, protein powder, chia and berries.
steps: Stir the oats, protein powder and chia seeds together in a jar.
Mix in the yoghurt and milk until smooth.
Top with the berries, cover and refrigerate overnight (at least 6 hours).
storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge. Make three jars at once for the week.
subs: Leave out the whey and use 250 g yoghurt instead.
Use soy yoghurt and soy milk for a dairy-free version.
Choose a halal-certified protein powder if required.

name: Spinach & feta egg-white omelette
desc: A light, fluffy egg-white omelette filled with spinach, feta and tomato, with wholemeal toast.
steps: Whisk the egg whites and whole egg with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Wilt the spinach in the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pour in the eggs, cook for 2-3 minutes, lifting the edges, until almost set.
Crumble over the feta, add the diced tomato, fold and cook 1 more minute.
Serve with two slices of toast.
storage: Best eaten fresh. Cooked omelette keeps 1 day in the fridge.
subs: Swap feta for cottage cheese for more protein and less fat.

name: Baked salmon, sweet potato & greens
desc: Oven-baked salmon fillets with roasted sweet potato and green beans.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Cube the sweet potato, toss with half the oil and roast for 25-30 minutes.
After 12 minutes, add the salmon fillets to the tray, season and roast for 12-15 minutes until the fish flakes.
Steam or boil the green beans for 4-5 minutes.
Plate with a squeeze of lemon.
storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat salmon gently or eat cold in a salad.
subs: Use cod or barramundi for a leaner fish.
Swap sweet potato for 150 g cooked rice per serving.

name: Chicken tikka wraps with yoghurt sauce
desc: Yoghurt-marinated tikka chicken in wholemeal wraps with a cool cucumber sauce.
steps: Mix 100 g of the yoghurt with the spice mix, salt and lemon juice; coat the sliced chicken and marinate 10 minutes (or overnight).
Cook the chicken in a hot pan or under the grill for 8-10 minutes, turning, until cooked through (74 °C).
Grate the cucumber into the remaining yoghurt with salt and mint.
Fill each wrap with spinach, sliced onion, chicken and sauce.
storage: Store chicken and sauce separately for up to 3 days; assemble wraps fresh.
subs: Use halal-certified chicken.
Use a gluten-free wrap if needed.
Use dairy-free yoghurt for the sauce.

name: Turkey bolognese with pasta
desc: A lean turkey and vegetable bolognese tossed through pasta.
steps: Finely chop the onion, carrot and mushrooms.
Soften the vegetables in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the mince and cook, breaking it up, until browned with no pink remaining (74 °C).
Add the tomatoes and dried herbs, simmer 20 minutes.
Cook the pasta in salted water as per the packet, drain and combine.
storage: Keeps 4 days refrigerated; sauce freezes well for 3 months.
subs: Use halal-certified turkey or beef mince.
Use lentils instead of mince for a vegan version.
Use gluten-free pasta if needed.

name: Crispy tofu & vegetable stir-fry
desc: Golden pan-fried tofu with mixed vegetables and edamame over rice.
steps: Press the tofu with a towel for 10 minutes, then cube it.
Fry the tofu in the oil over medium-high heat for 8 minutes, turning, until golden.
Add the vegetables and edamame and stir-fry for 4 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, toss and serve over the rice.
storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. Tofu softens on reheating but stays tasty.
subs: Use tamari for gluten-free.
Use halal-certified chicken breast instead of tofu for a meat version (cook to 74 °C).
Choose a soy sauce or tamari with no added alcohol if you follow a strict halal diet.

name: Tuna & chickpea protein salad
desc: A filling salad of tuna, chickpeas, crunchy vegetables and feta with a lemon dressing.
steps: Drain the tuna and chickpeas.
Chop the cucumber and tomato.
Toss everything with the oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper; crumble over the feta.
storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge in a sealed container; dress just before eating if possible.
subs: Leave out the feta for dairy-free.
Swap tuna for shredded cooked halal-certified chicken.

name: Cottage cheese, berries & almond snack bowl
desc: Creamy cottage cheese topped with berries, almonds and a drizzle of honey.
steps: Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl.
Roughly chop the almonds.
Top with the berries and almonds and drizzle with the honey.
storage: Best fresh; keeps 1 day covered in the fridge.
subs: Use Greek yoghurt instead of cottage cheese.
Use seeds instead of almonds for a nut-free version.

name: Red lentil & spinach dal
desc: A gently spiced red lentil, tomato and coconut dal with spinach and basmati rice.
steps: Soften the chopped onion in the oil with garlic and ginger for 5 minutes.
Add the spices for 1 minute, then the tomatoes, lentils and coconut milk.
Simmer 15 minutes, stir in the spinach until wilted.
Cook the rice and serve with the dal.
storage: Keeps 4 days refrigerated or 3 months frozen.
subs: Stir in 150 g Greek yoghurt per 2 servings at the end for extra protein (not vegan).
Add cooked halal-certified chicken for a higher-protein version.

name: Banana protein pancakes
desc: Fluffy banana-oat pancakes boosted with eggs and whey, topped with yoghurt and berries.
steps: Blend the oats, banana, eggs, egg whites and protein powder into a batter.
Cook ladlefuls in a lightly oiled non-stick pan over medium heat, 2 minutes per side.
Serve topped with yoghurt and berries.
storage: Cooked pancakes keep 2 days in the fridge or 1 month frozen; reheat in a toaster.
subs: Use gluten-free oats if needed.
Leave out whey and add 1 extra egg white.
Choose a halal-certified protein powder if required.

name: Lamb kofta with couscous & salad
desc: Spiced lamb koftas with couscous, fresh salad and garlic-mint yoghurt.
steps: Grate the onion and mix with the mince, cumin, coriander, salt and chopped parsley.
Shape into 12 sausages and grill or pan-fry for 10-12 minutes, turning, until cooked through (71 °C).
Prepare the couscous and chop the salad.
Serve with yoghurt mixed with garlic and mint.
storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated; freeze raw koftas for up to 3 months.
subs: Use halal-certified lamb.
Use 5% beef mince to reduce fat.

name: Garlic prawn & vegetable rice bowl
desc: Garlicky prawns stir-fried with broccoli and capsicum over rice.
steps: Stir-fry sliced garlic, broccoli and capsicum in the oil for 4 minutes.
Add the prawns and soy sauce and heat through for 2 minutes.
Serve over the rice.
storage: Eat within 2 days; reheat only once until piping hot.
subs: Shellfish allergy: use chicken or tofu instead.
Choose a soy sauce or tamari with no added alcohol if you follow a strict halal diet.

name: Scrambled eggs & smashed avocado on toast
desc: Fluffy high-protein scrambled eggs on wholemeal toast with lemony smashed avocado and tomato.
steps: Whisk the eggs and egg whites with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Mash the avocado with the lemon juice, a pinch of salt and chilli flakes.
Cook the eggs in a non-stick pan over low-medium heat, stirring gently, for 2-3 minutes until just set with no runny egg left.
Toast the bread, spread with the avocado and top with the eggs and sliced tomato.
storage: Best eaten fresh. Cooked eggs keep 1 day in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.
subs: Use gluten-free bread if needed.
Stir 50 g cottage cheese into the eggs for extra protein.

name: Freezer-friendly breakfast burritos
desc: Egg, black bean and cheddar burritos you can batch-cook and freeze for grab-and-go breakfasts.
steps: Dice the onion and capsicum and soften in the oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Whisk the eggs and egg whites with salt, pepper and 1 tsp smoked paprika, pour into the pan and stir gently for 3-4 minutes until fully set.
Stir through the drained, rinsed black beans and heat for 1 minute.
Divide the filling between the wraps, sprinkle with grated cheddar, fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Eat straight away, or cool quickly, wrap each burrito in baking paper and foil and refrigerate or freeze.
storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated or 2 months frozen. Remove the foil and microwave from frozen for 2-3 minutes, turning once, until piping hot in the centre.
subs: Use gluten-free wraps if needed.
Swap the cheddar for light mozzarella to trim the fat.
Add salsa or hot sauce when serving.

name: Greek yoghurt, berry & granola parfait
desc: Thick, protein-rich Greek yoghurt layered with berries and crunchy granola.
steps: Use fresh berries, or thaw frozen berries in the fridge overnight or for 1 minute in the microwave.
Layer half the yoghurt, half the berries and half the granola in a glass or jar.
Repeat the layers and eat straight away so the granola stays crunchy.
storage: Keep the yoghurt and berries in a sealed jar in the fridge for up to 2 days and add the granola just before eating.
subs: Many granolas contain nuts; choose a nut-free granola or toasted oats if needed.
Use soy yoghurt for dairy-free (protein will be lower).

name: Turmeric tofu scramble on toast
desc: A plant-based take on scrambled eggs with golden turmeric tofu, mushrooms and spinach.
steps: Pat the tofu dry with paper towel and crumble it into small pieces with your hands.
Cook the sliced mushrooms in the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat for 4 minutes until golden.
Add the tofu, 1/2 tsp ground turmeric, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, salt and pepper and cook for 4 minutes, stirring, until hot.
Stir through the spinach and diced tomato until the spinach wilts.
Toast the bread and pile the scramble on top.
storage: Keeps 2 days in a sealed container in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.
subs: Use gluten-free bread if needed.
Add a pinch of black salt (kala namak) for an eggy flavour.

name: Greek chicken wraps with tzatziki
desc: Lemon-oregano chicken, crisp salad, feta and garlicky tzatziki rolled in a wholemeal wrap.
steps: Grate 40 g of the cucumber, squeeze out the liquid and mix with the yoghurt, crushed garlic, half the lemon juice, salt and dried mint to make tzatziki.
Slice the cooked chicken and toss with the remaining lemon juice and 1 tsp dried oregano.
Slice the rest of the cucumber, the tomato and the lettuce.
Spread each wrap with tzatziki, add the lettuce, chicken, tomato and cucumber, crumble over the feta and roll up tightly.
storage: Use cooked chicken within 3 days of cooking. Keep the tzatziki separate and assemble just before eating; packed wraps should stay chilled below 5 °C and be eaten the same day.
subs: Use halal-certified chicken (leftover grilled breast works well); if cooking it fresh, cook to 74 °C.
Swap the chicken for 240 g drained chickpeas for a vegetarian wrap.
Use gluten-free wraps if needed.

name: Tuna, avocado & edamame rice bowl
desc: A poke-style bowl of tuna, avocado, edamame and corn over rice with a soy-lemon drizzle.
steps: Heat the rice (a microwave pouch, or leftover rice reheated until steaming hot) and divide between two bowls.
Cover the frozen edamame and corn with boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain.
Drain and flake the tuna; slice the avocado and cucumber.
Arrange everything over the rice and drizzle with the soy sauce and lemon juice.
storage: Best eaten fresh. Only use leftover rice that was refrigerated within 1 hour of cooking, and reheat it once only.
subs: Use tamari for gluten-free.
Choose a soy sauce or tamari with no added alcohol if you follow a strict halal diet.
Swap the tuna for 150 g firm tofu for a vegetarian bowl.

name: Mediterranean chickpea & quinoa salad
desc: A zesty lunchbox salad of quinoa, chickpeas, crunchy vegetables and feta.
steps: Rinse 240 g dry quinoa and simmer in 480 ml water, covered, for 12-15 minutes until the water is absorbed; spread out to cool.
Chop the cucumber, tomato and capsicum into small pieces.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, 1 tsp dried oregano, salt and pepper.
Toss the quinoa, drained chickpeas, vegetables and dressing together and crumble over the feta.
Divide into four containers.
storage: Keeps 3 days in sealed containers in the fridge.
subs: Leave out the feta for a vegan, dairy-free salad.
Add 100 g grilled halal-certified chicken per serve for extra protein.

name: Black bean & corn quesadillas
desc: Crisp wholemeal quesadillas filled with spiced black beans, corn, capsicum and melted cheddar.
steps: Mash half the drained beans with 1 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika and salt, then stir in the remaining beans, the corn and the diced capsicum.
Spread the filling over one half of each wrap, sprinkle with the grated cheddar and fold over.
Cook in a dry non-stick pan over medium heat for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and the cheese has melted.
Cut into wedges and serve with the yoghurt in place of sour cream.
storage: The filling keeps 3 days in the fridge. Cooked quesadillas keep 2 days; reheat in a dry pan until hot through.
subs: Use gluten-free wraps if needed.
Use dairy-free cheese and yoghurt for a vegan version.

name: Chicken thigh burrito bowls
desc: Smoky paprika chicken thighs with brown rice, beans, corn and fresh tomato salsa.
steps: Toss the chicken with half the oil, 2 tsp smoked paprika, 2 tsp ground cumin and salt.
Cook in a hot pan or on a grill for 5-6 minutes per side until the thickest part reaches 74 °C; rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Cook the sliced capsicum in the remaining oil for 4-5 minutes, and warm the drained beans and corn.
Dice the tomato and mix with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt for a quick salsa.
Divide the rice, chicken, beans, corn and capsicum between four containers; add the salsa and yoghurt when serving.
storage: Cool within 1 hour and refrigerate for up to 3 days, keeping the salsa and yoghurt separate. Reheat until piping hot throughout.
subs: Use halal-certified chicken.
Swap the chicken for 600 g firm tofu for a vegetarian bowl.
Use quinoa instead of brown rice.

name: Beef & broccoli stir-fry
desc: Tender strips of lean beef tossed with broccoli and capsicum in a garlic-ginger soy sauce.
steps: Slice the beef thinly across the grain and toss with 1 tbsp of the soy sauce.
Heat half the oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the beef in two batches for 1-2 minutes until browned; set aside.
Add the remaining oil, sliced onion, broccoli, capsicum and 2 tbsp water and stir-fry for 4 minutes until tender-crisp, adding the garlic and 1 tsp grated ginger for the last 30 seconds.
Return the beef with the remaining soy sauce and toss for 1 minute until everything is hot.
Serve over the rice or divide into containers.
storage: Cool within 1 hour and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat until piping hot throughout.
subs: Use halal-certified beef.
Choose a soy sauce or tamari with no added alcohol if you follow a strict halal diet.
Use tamari for gluten-free.
Swap the beef for sliced chicken breast (cook to 74 °C).

name: Chicken, pumpkin & spinach curry
desc: A mild coconut-tomato curry with tender chicken, sweet pumpkin and spinach, served with basmati rice.
steps: Soften the diced onion in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes, then add the garlic, 1 tsp grated ginger and the spice mix and cook for 1 minute.
Add the diced chicken and stir to coat for 3 minutes.
Add the pumpkin (2 cm cubes), tomatoes and coconut milk and simmer, partly covered, for 20 minutes until the pumpkin is tender and the chicken reaches 74 °C.
Meanwhile rinse the rice and cook it in 525 ml water, covered, on low heat for 12-15 minutes, then rest 5 minutes.
Stir the spinach through the curry until wilted and divide the curry and rice into five portions.
storage: Cool within 1 hour; keeps 4 days refrigerated or 3 months frozen. Reheat until piping hot throughout.
subs: Use halal-certified chicken.
Swap the chicken for 2 cans of drained chickpeas for a vegan curry.
Use sweet potato instead of pumpkin.

name: Lentil cottage pie with sweet potato mash
desc: A hearty vegetarian cottage pie of rich lentil and vegetable filling under a cheesy sweet potato mash.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Peel and chop the sweet potato, boil for 12-15 minutes until tender, drain and mash with the milk, salt and pepper.
Soften the diced onion, carrot and mushrooms in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the garlic and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, drained lentils and 1 tsp dried thyme and simmer for 10 minutes until thick; stir in the peas.
Spoon into a baking dish, spread the mash over the top and sprinkle with grated cheddar.
Bake for 20 minutes until golden and bubbling at the edges.
storage: Keeps 4 days refrigerated or 3 months frozen in portions. Reheat until piping hot throughout.
subs: Leave out the cheese and use soy milk for a vegan pie.
Use 500 g halal-certified lean beef mince instead of half the lentils.

name: Lemon-garlic fish with zucchini & quinoa
desc: Flaky white fish baked with lemon and garlic alongside roasted zucchini, tomatoes and quinoa.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Toss the sliced zucchini and halved tomatoes with half the oil, spread on a lined tray and roast for 5 minutes.
Mix the remaining oil, lemon juice, crushed garlic, salt and pepper and brush over the fish.
Add the fish to the tray and roast for 10-12 minutes until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily (63 °C at the thickest point).
Heat the quinoa (a microwave pouch, or 120 g dry quinoa simmered in 240 ml water for 15 minutes) and serve with the fish and vegetables.
storage: Best eaten fresh. Leftovers keep 2 days in the fridge; reheat gently until steaming hot.
subs: Barramundi, snapper or basa all work well.
Swap the quinoa for couscous or brown rice.

name: One-tray chicken & vegetable bake
desc: Garlic-lemon chicken thighs roasted on one tray with potatoes and colourful vegetables.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan). Cut the potatoes into 3 cm chunks and the carrots into batons, toss with half the oil and salt, and roast for 15 minutes.
Toss the chicken with the remaining oil, crushed garlic, lemon juice, 1 tsp dried oregano and 1 tsp paprika.
Add the chicken, capsicum, zucchini and onion wedges to the tray in a single layer.
Roast for 25 minutes until the vegetables are golden and the chicken reaches 74 °C at the thickest part.
Rest for 5 minutes and divide between four plates or containers.
storage: Cool within 1 hour and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat until piping hot throughout.
subs: Use halal-certified chicken.
Swap the chicken for 2 cans of drained chickpeas and 300 g firm tofu for a vegan tray bake.
Use sweet potato instead of potato.

name: Beef burger bowls with sweet potato wedges
desc: Juicy lean beef patties served bun-free over crisp salad with roasted sweet potato wedges.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C. Cut the sweet potato into wedges, toss with the oil, salt and paprika and roast for 25-30 minutes, turning halfway.
Mix the mince, egg, grated onion, salt and pepper and shape into 8 small patties.
Pan-fry or grill the patties for 4-5 minutes per side until cooked through with no pink in the centre (71 °C).
Divide the lettuce, tomato and cucumber between four bowls and top with the patties, grated cheddar, wedges and a little mustard.
storage: Cooked patties keep 3 days refrigerated; raw patties freeze for up to 3 months.
subs: Use halal-certified beef mince.
Use turkey mince for a leaner version (cook to 74 °C).
Serve in a wholemeal bun if you prefer.

name: Paneer tikka with rice & cucumber raita
desc: Spiced, charred paneer and vegetable skewers with fluffy basmati and cooling cucumber raita.
steps: Mix 100 g of the yoghurt with the spice mix, lemon juice and salt; toss with the cubed paneer, capsicum and onion chunks, drizzle with the oil and marinate for 15 minutes.
Thread onto skewers (soak wooden skewers for 20 minutes first) or spread on a lined tray.
Grill or bake at 220 °C for 12-15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges.
Meanwhile rinse the rice and cook it in 420 ml water, covered, on low heat for 12 minutes, then rest 5 minutes.
Grate the cucumber into the remaining yoghurt with salt and mint and serve with the paneer and rice.
storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated; keep the raita separate.
subs: Use firm tofu and soy yoghurt for a vegan version.
Use halal-certified chicken breast instead of paneer (cook to 74 °C).

name: Sticky tempeh, greens & peanut sauce bowl
desc: Golden tempeh glazed in a garlicky peanut sauce with steamed greens and brown rice.
steps: Cut the tempeh into 1 cm slices.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, lemon juice, crushed garlic and 3 tbsp hot water into a smooth sauce.
Fry the tempeh in the oil over medium-high heat for 3-4 minutes per side until golden, then add half the sauce and toss until sticky.
Steam the broccoli and green beans for 4-5 minutes until tender-crisp.
Serve the tempeh and greens over the rice and drizzle with the remaining sauce.
storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated; reheat until steaming hot.
subs: Use tamari for gluten-free.
Choose a soy sauce or tamari with no added alcohol if you follow a strict halal diet.
Peanut allergy: use tahini or sunflower seed butter.
Firm tofu works instead of tempeh.

name: Hummus & crunchy veg snack box
desc: A crunchy, colourful snack box of fresh vegetable sticks and rice cakes with creamy hummus.
steps: Cut the carrot, cucumber and capsicum into sticks.
Spoon the hummus into a small container.
Pack the vegetable sticks and rice cakes alongside for dipping.
storage: Cut vegetables keep 3 days in the fridge in a sealed container; keep rice cakes dry and separate.
subs: Sesame allergy: use a white bean dip instead of hummus.
Add a hard-boiled egg for extra protein.

name: Peanut butter protein balls
desc: No-bake oat, date and peanut butter bites boosted with protein powder.
steps: Cover the chopped dates with boiling water for 5 minutes to soften, then drain well.
Pulse the oats in a food processor until coarse, then add the protein powder and chia seeds.
Add the peanut butter, honey, dates and milk and process to a firm dough, adding a little more milk if crumbly.
Roll into 12 balls (2 per serving) and chill for 30 minutes until firm.
storage: Keeps 1 week in an airtight container in the fridge or 2 months frozen.
subs: Choose a halal-certified protein powder if required.
Nut-free: use sunflower seed butter.
Vegan: use pea protein, soy milk and maple syrup instead of whey, milk and honey.

name: Chilli-salt edamame
desc: Bright green edamame tossed with flaky salt, chilli and lemon for a plant-protein snack.
steps: Cook the frozen shelled edamame in boiling water for 3-4 minutes, or microwave as per the packet, until hot.
Drain well and toss with flaky salt, a pinch of chilli flakes and the lemon juice.
Serve warm or chilled.
storage: Cooked edamame keeps 3 days in the fridge; eat cold or reheat until steaming.
subs: Use edamame in the pod and double the cooking time for a slower snack.

name: Tuna & cottage cheese rice cakes
desc: Crisp rice cakes topped with a creamy tuna and cottage cheese mix and fresh tomato.
steps: Drain the tuna and mix with the cottage cheese, lemon juice and black pepper.
Spread the mixture over the rice cakes.
Top with sliced tomato and eat straight away so the rice cakes stay crisp.
storage: The tuna mix keeps 2 days in a sealed container in the fridge; assemble just before eating.
subs: Swap tuna for canned salmon.
Use Greek yoghurt instead of cottage cheese.

name: Frozen Greek yoghurt berry bark
desc: Frozen shards of honey-sweetened Greek yoghurt studded with berries and dark chocolate.
steps: Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Mix the yoghurt and honey and spread it about 1 cm thick over the paper.
Scatter over the berries, then melt the chocolate in 30-second bursts in the microwave and drizzle it over.
Freeze for at least 3 hours until firm, then break into 8 pieces (2 per serving).
storage: Keeps 1 month in an airtight container in the freezer; eat straight from the freezer.
subs: Check the chocolate label if you avoid dairy or need it to be nut-free.
Use maple syrup instead of honey.

name: Chocolate peanut butter protein shake
desc: A thick chocolate, banana and peanut butter shake with a big protein hit.
steps: Add the milk, protein powder, banana, peanut butter and cocoa to a blender.
Add a handful of ice and blend for 30-45 seconds until smooth.
Pour into a glass and drink straight away.
storage: Best fresh; keeps up to 24 hours covered in the fridge. Shake before drinking.
subs: Choose a halal-certified protein powder if required.
Use soy milk for dairy-free and pea protein instead of whey.

name: Mixed berry protein smoothie
desc: A creamy, tangy berry smoothie made with milk, Greek yoghurt and whey.
steps: Add the milk, protein powder, frozen berries and yoghurt to a blender.
Blend for 30-45 seconds until smooth, adding a splash of water if too thick.
Pour into a glass and drink straight away.
storage: Best fresh; keeps up to 24 hours covered in the fridge. Shake before drinking.
subs: Choose a halal-certified protein powder if required.
Use soy milk, soy yoghurt and pea protein for a dairy-free version.

name: Mango oat vegan protein shake
desc: A tropical dairy-free shake of mango, oats, soy milk and pea protein.
steps: Add the soy milk, pea protein, frozen mango and oats to a blender.
Blend for 45-60 seconds until completely smooth.
Pour into a glass and drink straight away.
storage: Best fresh; keeps up to 24 hours covered in the fridge. Shake before drinking.
subs: Use gluten-free oats if needed.
Swap mango for banana or pineapple.
